# What Is the Technical Substrate? <br> Representations, Methods, and Tools

Building reliable AI-assisted design loops requires a rigorous technical substrate. We cannot simply connect language models to hardware code generators and hope for correct silicon. In Part II, we define *What* technical building blocks comprise Architecture 2.0, spanning machine-usable hardware representations, learned design methods, tool-connected execution environments, and formal verification feedback.

We classify structural hardware representations across ASTs, CDFGs, SystemC TLM 2.0, and PDK NDA abstractions. Furthermore, we connect generative models and Bayesian optimizers to cycle-accurate simulators (gem5, FireSim) and physical design EDA tools (OpenROAD, Synopsys VCS), constructing formal verification checkers (SVA, UPF PST) to detect and eliminate proxy gaming.

::: {.callout-note icon=false appearance="simple"}
1. How do we maintain machine-usable state alignment between learned surrogate models and version-controlled hardware records?
2. What mechanisms prevent AI search algorithms from exploiting unmodeled physical edge cases in fast evaluation proxies?
:::
